segments.text: Euclid's Elements, Book One, Proposition Twenty. In any triangle, the sum of any two sides is greater than the remaining side. Given triangle A B C, we prove that any two of its sides taken together are greater than the third side.

segments.text: Extend side B A to point D so that segment A D equals side A C, and construct segment D C.

segments.text: Since A D equals A C in isosceles triangle A D C, base angle A D C equals angle A C D. Because the whole angle B C D is greater than its part A C D, angle B C D is also greater than angle A D C. In triangle D B C, the greater angle B C D is subtended by the greater side, so D B is greater than B C. Since D B is the sum of B A and A D, and A D equals A C, sides B A and A C together are greater than B C, and similarly for the other pairs, as was required to prove.
